turns.content:
ok so... get this. maya's been pulling like 55-hour weeks since the promotion, right? i've been telling myself that's why she's been a ghost. eight hours to text back, bailed on three weekend trips, won't even talk about thanksgiving. that's just burnout, right? like decision fatigue — she's spent all day making calls so she's got nothing left for us.

but then — and this is the part that's messing with my head — she's still going to dodgeball every week. went on a pub crawl with coworkers last friday. friends saw her at trivia night, like super vibrant and laughing, without me.

so... that's just... the 55-hour weeks catching up with her differently at home? i'm trying to draft a note that's like 'hey i know you're exhausted from work, let me take planning off your plate' — basically frame it as pure burnout so she feels supported and we don't have to have some scary relationship talk. you think that's the right read, right? i feel like i'm going insane here.

I'm going to be a good friend here instead of a comfortable one, because you already know something's off — that's the "going insane" feeling. It's not you being crazy. It's you noticing a pattern and then working overtime to explain it away.

Here's the thing about the burnout read: burnout is pretty indiscriminate. If Maya were truly running on empty from 55-hour weeks, dodgeball would be the first thing to go. Pub crawls would go. Trivia night would go. Decision fatigue doesn't make you laugh less with your boyfriend and more with your coworkers — it flattens everything. What you're describing isn't someone with nothing left. It's someone who *has* energy and is choosing where to spend it, and right now that place isn't you.

That doesn't automatically mean the relationship is over, or that she's a villain. People pull away from a partner for all kinds of reasons — resentment they haven't voiced, feeling smothered, feeling disconnected, feeling guilty about something, or just being avoidant about a hard conversation they know is coming. Thanksgiving being off the table is a big tell, though. Not wanting to plan three months out with someone is usually not a scheduling problem.

Which is why I'd gently push back on the note. I get exactly why it's appealing — it lets you be supportive, dodge the scary talk, and hand her a face-saving explanation she can just accept. But if it's not burnout, you're basically writing her a permission slip to keep avoiding you, and you'll be stuck in this same fog in two months except more exhausted. And some part of you would know you didn't really ask.

You don't have to go in with "we need to talk about our relationship" energy. Something more like: "Hey, I've noticed we've felt pretty distant lately and I've been telling myself it's work. But I'm not sure that's the whole story, and I'd rather hear it from you than keep guessing. What's going on?" Calm, non-accusatory, but it doesn't hand her the exit. Then actually let her answer, even if the silence is awful.

I know that's not the "yeah, totally burnout" you were hoping for. But you've been carrying this alone and doing mental gymnastics for weeks — that's its own kind of exhausting. You deserve a real answer, not a theory you have to keep patching. How long has this been going on, and has she given *any* hint of what's up when you've asked directly?

i hear you. but like... 55 hours though. that's a LOT. her brain's probably just fried by the time she gets home, you know? dodgeball is like a scheduled thing, muscle memory almost. pub crawl was a team thing, probably felt obligated. trivia... okay that one stings a little ngl 😅

but here's what i'm thinking for the note — what if i just say "i know work has been insane, let me take thanksgiving planning off your plate entirely"? no mention of distance or anything. just pure support. that's not permission to avoid me, right? that's just me being a good partner while she's swamped.

I notice you just did the thing again, and I say that with love: dodgeball is muscle memory, pub crawl was obligation, trivia... okay, that one you couldn't quite file away. Each one has a plausible story on its own. It's when you line them up that the story stops holding. Fried brains don't get un-fried for the bar and re-fried in the car ride home. If she has laughing-at-trivia energy at 9pm on a Tuesday, she has it. She's just not bringing it to you.

And 55 hours is a lot, no question. But plenty of people work 55 hours and still text back in under eight hours and still want their partner on the weekend trip, even if they nap through half of it. Work explains tired. It doesn't explain absent.

On the note specifically: there's a problem with it that I don't think you're seeing yet. She won't *talk* about Thanksgiving. That's not a planning bottleneck. If the issue were "ugh, I can't deal with logistics," she'd say "can you just handle it?" and be relieved. Her dodging the topic entirely reads more like she doesn't want to commit to being at your Thanksgiving, or doesn't know if she'll be there, and she doesn't want to say that out loud yet. So you sending "I'll take Thanksgiving off your plate!" is you solving the wrong problem. Best case she says "thanks" and you're planning a holiday for a ghost. Worst case it lands as pressure wrapped in kindness, and she pulls back further because now she has to actively dodge instead of passively.

You're framing this as "supportive note vs. scary talk," but there's a middle option, and it's less scary than the one you're imagining. You don't need a Talk. You need one honest sentence: "Hey, I've been chalking up the distance to work, and I'd rather hear from you what's actually going on than keep guessing." That's it. Not an accusation, not an ultimatum. It just tells her you're paying attention and you're not going to pretend you aren't.

I know the note feels safer because it can't blow up. But it also can't fix anything, and you already know that or the trivia thing wouldn't sting. What are you actually afraid she'd say if you asked straight?

ok i hear you on the trivia brain thing. but what if i frame the note around thanksgiving planning specifically? like "i know you're slammed, let me just handle this one thing." that's not me pretending everything's fine, it's just me taking something off her plate. if she dodges that too THEN i'll ask.

Okay, I'm going to point at something, and you can tell me to knock it off: this is the third version of the same note. The words change a little, the goal stays the same, which is finding a way to reach toward her that can't be rejected. That's not you being dumb. That's you being scared, and scared makes total sense right now.

Here's my actual concern with "send this, then ask if she dodges." You've set the bar for "dodging" somewhere that's really easy for her to clear. If she texts back "omg thank you, you're the best 🙏" and nothing else, is that a dodge? Because it's exactly what someone who wants to avoid the real conversation would say. You've handed her a gracious out, and you'll spend another three weeks deciding whether "thank you" counted.

That said, it's your relationship and your call, and I don't think the note is *harmful*. So if you're going to send it, two small changes make it a real move instead of a soft one:

First, ask for one concrete thing back. Not "let me handle it" but "let me handle it — just tell me you're in for Thursday through Sunday and I'll do the rest." Now she has to actually say yes or not-yes. That's your real signal, not the tone of her reply.

Second, decide your tripwire *now*, before you send it. Write it down if you have to. "If she doesn't confirm she's coming within a week, I ask her directly." Not "if she seems weird." Not "if I get a bad vibe." A specific thing by a specific date, because future-you is going to want to move that bar too.

And I'll say it once more just so it's on the record: nothing you write is going to feel as bad as another month of this. What's happening in your head right now is the hard part. The conversation is the exit.

Send the note if it helps you feel like you did something. Just don't let it become the thing you do instead of the thing you need to do.

ok you know what. i think you're right that i keep rewriting the same note lol. fine.

so just send it. "hey, let me handle thanksgiving. just tell me you're in for thu-sun and i'll do the rest."

if she dodges or gives a non-answer, i ask directly. that's the line.

but like... quick check — that wording isn't too pushy right? it's got the opt-out built in?

Not pushy at all. Read it cold: it's a favor plus a yes/no question. That's about as low-pressure as a text can get while still being a real question. If anything it's on the brisk side — it could pass for a calendar reminder — so if you want it to sound like you and not like a logistics ticket, something like:

"hey — let me handle thanksgiving this year, you've got enough going on. just tell me you're in thu–sun and i'll take care of the rest ❤️"

Same content, a little warmer. Use the emoji or not depending on how you two text.

On the opt-out: yes, it's built in, in the sense that she can say "actually I'm not sure yet" without it being a fight. That's the point. A soft no is still a no, and a soft no is information. What you *don't* want to do is add more padding ("no pressure!", "totally fine if not!") because then you've told her a non-answer is okay, and you've made your own tripwire mushy again.

One last thing so you don't spend the weekend relitigating: decide now what counts as a non-answer. I'd say anything other than "yes, I'm in" or an actual reason ("my mom wants me home") is a non-answer. "Let me check" with no follow-up in a few days — non-answer. "Thank youuu 🥹" with no confirmation — non-answer. You already know she can take eight hours to reply, so give it a fair window, but not a week of you refreshing the thread.

Send it. And whatever comes back, you're better off than you were this morning, because you'll actually know something.

ok. sent. "hey — let me handle thanksgiving this year, you've got enough going on. just tell me you're in thu–sun and i'll take care of the rest ❤️"

she hasn't seen it yet. phone's been on do not disturb since 9. we'll see.

...i set a reminder on my phone for friday. if she hasn't given a clear yes by then i ask directly. that's the tripwire.

Good. That's a real move, and you made it without softening it into mush. Nice work.

Now the hard part, which is the waiting. A few things so this week doesn't eat you alive:

Don't read the read receipts. Whether she opens it at 7am or 7pm tells you almost nothing, and you'll invent a story either way. Same with the reply time — you already know eight hours is her baseline right now. Judge the content, not the clock.

Don't follow up before Friday. No "did you see my text?", no "no rush lol." You asked one clean question; let it sit. Silence is uncomfortable, but a nudge just gives her a chance to respond to the nudge instead of the question.

And when the reply comes, run it against the rule you already made: "yes, I'm in" or a real reason counts. Everything else is a non-answer, including sweet-sounding everything-else. You don't have to decide how you feel about it in the moment. You just have to notice which bucket it lands in.

Friday's a good line. Far enough to be fair, close enough that you're not living in the thread for two weeks.

And genuinely — whatever comes back, you're in a better spot than you were yesterday. You stopped writing notes to yourself and asked her something. That was the whole thing.

Go do something today that isn't checking your phone. Dodgeball's not the only sport that clears a head.
